component.name: Tessarium
component.summary: A private address for every 3 m square on Earth

description.p: Tessarium gives every ~3 m square on Earth an address made of three ordinary words and a four-digit number. The mapping from squares to addresses is derived from a seed phrase you hold, so two people with different phrases see different addresses for the same place, and an address means nothing to anyone without the phrase it was made under.

The core that turns a point into an address is written in F* and machine-checked: theorems establish that every point lies inside the square it maps to, that distinct squares get distinct addresses, and that decoding an address returns the square it was made from. The same proved source builds both the desktop program and the browser client.
The application runs a small server on your own machine and opens your browser to it. Nothing listens outside the loopback interface.
